reasoning: Evidence shows JNIM has imposed an economic blockade on Bamako since September 2025, causing fuel shortages and severe hardship. However, multiple sources emphasize JNIM lacks capacity to govern Mali and take physical control of the capital. The ICG warns of fragmentation risks if JNIM overextends. While analysts warn of potential terrorist takeover by 2026, this is speculative. The blockade strategy appears designed for economic suffocation rather than military conquest. With ~6,000 combatants spread across multiple countries and Mali's military receiving Russian support, a full takeover of a 3-4 million person capital by June 2026 (87 days away) appears unlikely. No evidence suggests imminent military assault on Bamako itself.
